042/**
043 * Used to denote that a class is a REST resource and to associate metadata on it.
044 *
045 * <p>
046 * Usually used on a subclass of {@link RestServlet}, but can be used to annotate any class that you want to expose as
047 * a REST resource.
048 *
049 * <h5 class='section'>Default response format (content negotiation):</h5>
050 * <p>
051 * The response format is <b>not</b> hardwired to JSON.  The serializer used to render a response body is chosen by
052 * ordinary HTTP content negotiation &mdash; the request's <c>Accept</c> header is best-matched against the media types
053 * of the configured {@link #serializers() serializers} (see {@link Serializer#getMediaTypeRanges()}).  A request that
054 * sends no <c>Accept</c> header (or a non-specific one such as <c>*&#47;*</c>, which browsers send by default) is
055 * treated as <c>*&#47;*</c> and matches the <b>first</b> serializer in the set.
056 *
057 * <p>
058 * In the default configuration ({@link BasicRestServlet} / {@link BasicRestResource}, via
059 * {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.config.BasicUniversalConfig}) the serializer set lists HTML first, so a browser
060 * &mdash; or any client that omits <c>Accept</c> &mdash; receives <b>HTML</b>, not JSON.  To always get JSON, send an
061 * explicit <c>Accept: application/json</c> header.  See {@link #serializers()} for how serializer ordering determines
062 * this default.
063 *
064 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
065 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestAnnotatedClasses">@Rest-Annotated Class Basics</a>
066
067 * </ul>
068 */
069@Target(TYPE)
070@Retention(RUNTIME)
071@Inherited
072@AnnotationGroup(Rest.class)
073public @interface Rest {
074
075   /**
076    * Allowed header URL parameters.
077    *
078    * <p>
079    * When specified, allows headers such as <js>"Accept"</js> and <js>"Content-Type"</js> to be passed in as URL query
080    * parameters.
081    * <br>
082    * For example:
083    * <p class='burlenc'>
084    *  ?Accept=text/json&amp;Content-Type=text/json
085    * </p>
086    *
087    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
088    *    <li class='note'>
089    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
090    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
091    *    <li class='note'>
092    *       Use <js>"*"</js> to represent all methods.
093    *    <li class='note'>
094    *       Use <js>"NONE"</js> (case insensitive) to suppress inheriting a value from a parent class.
095    * </ul>
096    *
097    * @return The annotation value.
098    */
099   String allowedHeaderParams() default "";
100
101   /**
102    * Allowed method headers.
103    *
104    * <p>
105    * A comma-delimited list of HTTP method names that are allowed to be passed as values in an <c>X-Method</c>,
106    * <c>X-HTTP-Method-Override</c>, <c>X-HTTP-Method</c> or <c>X-Method-Override</c> HTTP header to override the real HTTP
107    * method name.  All four headers share this list; when more than one is sent they are tried in that order.
108    * <p>
109    * Allows you to override the actual HTTP method with a simulated method.
110    * <br>For example, if an HTTP Client API doesn't support <c>PATCH</c> but does support <c>POST</c> (because
111    * <c>PATCH</c> is not part of the original HTTP spec), you can add a <c>X-Method: PATCH</c> header on a normal
112    * <c>HTTP POST /foo</c> request call which will make the HTTP call look like a <c>PATCH</c> request in any of the REST APIs.
113    *
114    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
115    *    <li class='note'>
116    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
117    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
118    *    <li class='note'>
119    *       Method names are case-insensitive.
120    *    <li class='note'>
121    *       Use <js>"*"</js> to represent all methods.
122    *    <li class='note'>
123    *       Use <js>"NONE"</js> (case insensitive) to suppress inheriting a value from a parent class.
124    *    <li class='note'>
125    *       Once the list admits at least one method, override claims must agree: a request whose override headers (or
126    *       <c>method</c> query parameter) name more than one distinct method is refused with <c>400</c>, whether or not the
127    *       list admits them.
128    *    <li class='note'>
129    *       On a safe request (<c>GET</c>, <c>HEAD</c>, <c>OPTIONS</c>, <c>TRACE</c>), an override is honored only when it names
130    *       another safe method or an operation declared {@link RestOp#read() read=true}; anything else is refused with
131    *       <c>405</c>.  Overrides on a <c>POST</c> are unaffected.
132    * </ul>
133    *
134    * @return The annotation value.
135    */
136   String allowedMethodHeaders() default "";
137
138   /**
139    * Allowed method parameters.
140    *
141    * <p>
142    * When specified, the HTTP method can be overridden by passing in a <js>"method"</js> URL parameter.
143    * <br>
144    * For example:
145    * <p class='burlenc'>
146    *  ?method=OPTIONS
147    * </p>
148    * <p>
149    * On a safe request (<c>GET</c>, <c>HEAD</c>, <c>OPTIONS</c>, <c>TRACE</c>), which is what a link or a typed URL sends,
150    * the parameter may only name another safe method or a custom method whose operation is declared
151    * {@link RestOp#read() read=true}.  Anything else, for example <c>GET /foo?method=DELETE</c>, is refused with
152    * <c>405 Method Not Allowed</c>, so a link can never trigger a write.  On a <c>POST</c>, the parameter may name any
153    * method in this list.
154    *
155    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
156    *    <li class='note'>
157    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
158    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
159    *    <li class='note'>
160    *       Use <js>"*"</js> to represent all methods.
161    *    <li class='note'>
162    *       Use <js>"NONE"</js> (case insensitive) to suppress inheriting a value from a parent class.
163    * </ul>
164    *
165    * @return The annotation value.
166    */
167   String allowedMethodParams() default "";
168
169   /**
170    * Resource-level authenticator.
171    *
172    * <p>
173    * Resolves the {@link java.security.Principal} and roles for requests to this resource and its descendant child
174    * resources (inherited unless cut off via {@code noInherit={"authenticator"}}), so that {@code roleGuard} /
175    * {@link RoleBasedRestGuard} / {@link Auth @Auth}
176    * / {@code isUserInRole} resolve against the computed identity.
177    *
178    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
179    *    <li class='note'>
180    *       The implementation is instantiated through the resource's bean store (constructor injection).
181    *    <li class='note'>
182    *       The default {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.auth.RestAuthenticator.Null RestAuthenticator.Null} sentinel means &quot;not specified.&quot;
183    * </ul>
184    *
185    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
186    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerAuthenticator">REST Authenticator</a>
187    * </ul>
188    *
189    * @return The annotation value.
190    * @since 10.0.0
191    */
192   Class<? extends RestAuthenticator> authenticator() default RestAuthenticator.Null.class;
193
194   /**
195    * REST children.
196    *
197    * <p>
198    * Defines children of this resource.  Each child resource is mounted under its own URL subtree (per the
199    * child's own {@code @Rest(path=...)} / {@code @Rest(paths=...)}) and constructs its own {@link RestContext}.
200    *
201    * <h5 class='section'>Children vs. mixins (resolution semantics)</h5>
202    * <p>
203    * Children are <b>isolated from the parent's resolution chain</b> by design — a child's serializers, parsers,
204    * guards, hooks, etc. are all resolved against the child's own {@link RestContext} only, NOT walked
205    * through the parent.  This is the opposite of how {@link #mixins() mixins} resolve.  See the
206    * <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerMixinSubContexts#mixin-vs-child-divergence">Mixin Sub-Contexts &mdash; Mixin-vs-child divergence</a>
207    * topic for the rationale (children own their lifecycle and are externally mounted; mixins are inline composers
208    * sharing the host's URL namespace and resolution chain).
209    *
210    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
211    * <ul>
212    *    <li>Children on child are combined with those on parent class.
213    *    <li>Children are list parent-to-child in the order they appear in the annotation.
214    * </ul>
215    *
216    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
217    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/ChildResources">Child Resources</a>
218    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerMixinSubContexts">Mixin Sub-Contexts</a> (for the mixin-vs-child divergence)
219    * </ul>
220    *
221    * @return The annotation value.
222    */
223   Class<?>[] children() default {};
224
225   /**
226    * Rich child definitions &mdash; the host-side seed form of {@link #children()}.
227    *
228    * <p>
229    * Each {@link Child @Child} entry names a child class (via {@link Child#type()}) <b>and</b> lets the host
230    * seed a curated set of {@code @Rest}-level settings onto that child's otherwise-isolated
231    * {@link RestContext} &mdash; guards, role guards, part serializer/parser, and a
232    * handful of default-scalar settings &mdash; without editing the child class.
233    *
234    * <p>
235    * Unlike {@link #mixinDefs() mixinDefs}, this does not override an inherited chain (children never inherit
236    * from the host); it seeds settings onto an isolated context. Additive-security seed members ({@code guards},
237    * {@code converters}, {@code roleGuard}, {@code rolesDeclared}) can't be removed or weakened by the child;
238    * the remaining scalar seed members are a fallback the child's own explicit {@code @Rest} declaration wins
239    * over. See {@link Child} for the full semantics.
240    *
241    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
242    * <p class='bjava'>
243    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
244    *       childrenDefs=<ja>@Child</ja>(type=FooChild.<jk>class</jk>, maxInput=<js>"10M"</js>)
245    *    )
246    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource { ... }
247    * </p>
248    *
249    * <p>
250    * This attribute is additive to {@link #children()}: bare-class entries in {@code children()} and rich
251    * entries here are discovered together (bare classes first, then {@code childrenDefs}). A
252    * {@code @Child(type=X.class)} with no seed members is the exact equivalent of a bare
253    * {@code children=X.class} entry.
254    *
255    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
256    *    <li class='ja'>{@link Child}
257    *    <li class='jm'>{@link #children()}
258    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/ChildResources#host-side-seeding-with-child-1000">Child Resources &mdash; Host-side seeding with @Child</a>
259    * </ul>
260    *
261    * @return The annotation value.
262    * @since 10.0.0
263    */
264   Child[] childrenDefs() default {};
265
266   /**
267    * REST mixins.
268    *
269    * <p>
270    * Defines operation-provider classes whose {@link RestOp @RestOp}-group methods should be composed into this
271    * resource.
272    *
273    * <p>
274    * Mixin methods are discovered the same way as local operation methods and surface under this resource's URL
275    * namespace.  On path/method collisions, local methods on this resource win over mixin methods.
276    *
277    * <h5 class='section'>Per-mixin RestContext + host-to-mixin inheritance (since 10.0.0)</h5>
278    * <p>
279    * Each mixin class is elevated to its own {@link RestContext} parent-linked to this host's {@link RestContext}.
280    * The mixin's class-level {@code @Rest(...)} configuration applies to its own endpoints, with inheritance from
281    * the host:
282    * <ul>
283    *    <li><b>List-shaped properties</b> ({@code serializers}, {@code parsers}, {@code encoders}, {@code converters},
284    *       {@code responseProcessors}, {@code restOpArgs}, {@code guards}) — host's chain runs first, then the mixin's
285    *       appended.  Host endpoints see only the host's chain.
286    *    <li><b>Replace-shaped properties</b> ({@code partSerializer}, {@code partParser}) — the mixin's value wins
287    *       over the host's for mixin endpoints when declared; otherwise the host's value is inherited.
288    *    <li><b>{@code messages}</b> — the mixin's bundle is chained as a child of the host's via
289    *       {@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.cp.Messages#chain Messages.chain(child, parent)} so mixin keys win and missing
290    *       keys fall through to the host.
291    *    <li><b>Lifecycle hooks</b> ({@code @RestStartCall}, {@code @RestEndCall}, {@code @RestPreCall},
292    *       {@code @RestPostCall}, {@code @RestDestroy}) — dual-fire host-then-mixin for mixin-endpoint requests;
293    *       host-only for host-endpoint requests.
294    * </ul>
295    *
296    * <p>
297    * Use {@link #noInherit() @Rest(noInherit=&#123;...&#125;)} on a mixin class to cut off inheritance for a specific
298    * property — same token set as the host's {@code noInherit} machinery (e.g. {@code "serializers"},
299    * {@code "guards"}, {@code "messages"}).
300    *
301    * <h5 class='section'>Mixins vs. children</h5>
302    * <p>
303    * Mixins are inline composers that share the host's URL namespace and inherit from the host's resolution chain.
304    * {@link #children() Children} are independently-mounted resources isolated from the host's resolution chain.
305    * See the
306    * <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerMixinSubContexts#mixin-vs-child-divergence">Mixin Sub-Contexts &mdash; Mixin-vs-child divergence</a>
307    * topic for the rationale.
308    *
309    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
310    * <ul>
311    *    <li>Mixins on child are combined with those on parent class.
312    *    <li>Mixins are listed parent-to-child in the order they appear in the annotation.
313    *    <li>Transitive mixins ({@code A} mixes in {@code B}) parent-link flat to the host — both {@code A} and
314    *       {@code B} get {@code parentContext = host}, never an {@code A → B} chain.
315    * </ul>
316    *
317    * <p>
318    * For host-side per-mixin setting overrides (applying guards / serializers / a mount path / etc. to a
319    * specific mixin's endpoints without editing the mixin class), see the rich {@link #mixinDefs() mixinDefs}
320    * companion attribute.
321    *
322    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
323    *    <li class='jma'>{@link #mixinDefs()}
324    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerComposition">REST Server &mdash; Mixins and Multi-Mount Paths</a>
325    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerMixinSubContexts">REST Server &mdash; Mixin Sub-Contexts</a>
326    * </ul>
327    *
328    * @return The annotation value.
329    */
330   Class<?>[] mixins() default {};
331
332   /**
333    * Rich mixin definitions &mdash; the host-side override form of {@link #mixins()}.
334    *
335    * <p>
336    * Each {@link Mixin @Mixin} entry names a mixin class (via {@link Mixin#type()}) <b>and</b> lets the host
337    * override selected {@code @Rest}-level settings for that mixin's mixed-in endpoints &mdash; guards, role
338    * guards, serializers, default headers, mount path, etc. &mdash; without subclassing or editing the mixin
339    * class.
340    *
341    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
342    * <p class='bjava'>
343    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
344    *       mixinDefs=<ja>@Mixin</ja>(type=FooMixin.<jk>class</jk>, guards=AdminGuard.<jk>class</jk>)
345    *    )
346    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource { ... }
347    * </p>
348    *
349    * <p>
350    * This attribute is additive to {@link #mixins()}: bare-class entries in {@code mixins()} and rich entries
351    * here are discovered together (bare classes first, then {@code mixinDefs}).  A {@code @Mixin(type=X.class)}
352    * with no overrides is the exact equivalent of a bare {@code mixins=X.class} entry.
353    *
354    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
355    *    <li class='ja'>{@link Mixin}
356    *    <li class='jm'>{@link #mixins()}
357    * </ul>
358    *
359    * @return The annotation value.
360    * @since 10.0.0
361    */
362   Mixin[] mixinDefs() default {};
363
364   /**
365    * Mixin-declared opt-in: fold this class's own {@link #responseProcessors() responseProcessors} into the
366    * <b>host</b> resource's chain whenever this class is composed as a mixin via a plain
367    * {@link #mixins() @Rest(mixins=...)} reference.
368    *
369    * <p>
370    * By default ({@code false}) a mixin's {@code responseProcessors} apply only to the mixin's own endpoints
371    * &mdash; a host's own {@code @RestOp} methods see only the host's chain (the standard {@link #mixins() mixin}
372    * inheritance rule "host's chain runs first, then the mixin's appended; host endpoints see only the host's
373    * chain").  Setting this to {@code true} <b>on the mixin class itself</b> makes a plain
374    * {@code @Rest(mixins=ThisClass.class)} reference additionally append this class's own
375    * {@code responseProcessors} to the end of the host's own chain, so the host's own endpoints pick them up too.
376    *
377    * <p>
378    * This is the mixin-declared, response-processor-scoped counterpart to
379    * {@link Mixin#mergeIntoHost() @Mixin(mergeIntoHost=true)} (which is host-declared and folds <i>all</i>
380    * list-shaped attributes).  Unlike {@code mergeIntoHost}, this directive lives with the mixin and folds
381    * <b>only</b> {@code responseProcessors} &mdash; never {@code guards}, {@code serializers}, or any other
382    * list-shaped attribute.  It is intended for view-renderer mixins (e.g. {@code FreemarkerMixin}) so that
383    * declaring the mixin is enough to route the host's own {@code View} returns through the renderer.
384    *
385    * <p>
386    * Strictly opt-in and non-silent: it has no effect for a mixin that leaves it {@code false}, so existing
387    * mixins keep today's scoping exactly.  Same-class de-duplication applies, so a response processor the host
388    * already declares is not added twice.
389    *
390    * @return The annotation value.
391    * @since 10.0.0
392    */
393   boolean mergeResponseProcessorsIntoHost() default false;
394
395   /**
396    * Client version header.
397    *
398    * <p>
399    * Specifies the name of the header used to denote the client version on HTTP requests.
400    *
401    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
402    *    <li class='note'>
403    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
404    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
405    * </ul>
406    *
407    * @return The annotation value.
408    */
409   String clientVersionHeader() default "";
410
411   /**
412    * Optional location of configuration file for this servlet.
413    *
414    * <p>
415    * The configuration file .
416    *
417    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
418    * <ul>
419    *    <li>Config file is searched for in child-to-parent order.
420    * </ul>
421    *
422    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
423    *    <li class='note'>
424    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
425    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
426    *    <li class='note'>
427    *       Use the keyword <c>SYSTEM_DEFAULT</c> to refer to the system default configuration
428    *       returned by the {@link Config#getSystemDefault()}.
429    * </ul>
430    *
431    * @return The annotation value.
432    */
433   String config() default "";
434
435   /**
436    * Eagerly initializes framework-managed memoizers during {@link RestContext} construction.
437    *
438    * <p>
439    * When enabled, framework bean memoizers and operation/child-context memoizers are force-fired inside the
440    * constructor try/catch so startup-time configuration errors fail fast.
441    *
442    * <p>
443    * This setting is disabled by default.
444    *
445    * <ul class='values'>
446    *    <li><js>"true"</js> - Force eager initialization during context construction.
447    *    <li><js>"false"</js> - Keep initialization lazy until first use (default).
448    * </ul>
449    *
450    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
451    *    <li class='note'>
452    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
453    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
454    * </ul>
455    *
456    * @return The annotation value.
457    */
458   String eagerInit() default "";
459
460   /**
461    * Opt this parent resource into deferred (first-invocation) construction of its {@link #children()} sub-resources.
462    *
463    * <p>
464    * When {@code "true"}, the {@link RestContext} instances for all {@code @Rest(children=...)} entries are
465    * <em>not</em> built at parent startup.  Instead, each child's routing entry is registered immediately (so URL
466    * matching is fully operational from the first request), but the full {@link RestContext} — including all of its
467    * bean-store setup, memoizers, and lifecycle hooks — is constructed on the first inbound request to that child's
468    * URL prefix.  Subsequent requests reuse the already-built context.
469    *
470    * <p>
471    * This is particularly useful when a parent resource exposes heavyweight admin or diagnostic children that are
472    * rarely invoked in production.  Setting {@code lazyChildren="true"} on the parent lets the parent boot fast;
473    * each child pays its construction cost only when (and if) it is first accessed.
474    *
475    * <ul class='values'>
476    *    <li><js>"true"</js> - Children are constructed on first invocation (deferred).
477    *    <li><js>"false"</js> (default) - Children are constructed eagerly at parent startup.
478    * </ul>
479    *
480    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
481    *    <li class='note'>
482    *       The first request to a lazy child pays the full construction cost, which can be significant for
483    *       heavyweight children.  If predictable first-request latency is required, do not opt in.
484    *    <li class='note'>
485    *       Concurrent first-requests to the same lazy child are serialized: only one thread runs the construction;
486    *       others block until it completes.
487    *    <li class='note'>
488    *       A lazy child that is never invoked is never constructed.  Its lifecycle {@code @RestDestroy} / shutdown
489    *       hooks are skipped at parent destruction time.
490    *    <li class='note'>
491    *       The programmatic knob {@link RestContext.Builder#lazyChildInit(boolean)} overrides this annotation.
492    *    <li class='note'>
493    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
494    *       (e.g. <js>"$E{LAZY_CHILDREN,false}"</js>).
495    * </ul>
496    *
497    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
498    *    <li class='jm'>{@link RestContext.Builder#lazyChildInit(boolean)}
499    *    <li class='jm'>{@link #children()}
500    * </ul>
501    *
502    * @return The annotation value.
503    */

562   /**
563    * Property names for which less-derived contributions are NOT inherited.
564    *
565    * <p>
566    * Accepted values include {@code "allowedParserOptions"}, {@code "allowedSerializerOptions"},
567    * {@code "allowedHeaderParams"}, {@code "allowedMethodHeaders"}, {@code "allowedMethodParams"},
568    * {@code "disableContentParam"}, {@code "renderResponseStackTraces"}, {@code "problemDetails"},
569    * {@code "debugMarshalling"},
570    * {@code "eagerInit"}, {@code "lazyChildren"}, {@code "clientVersionHeader"},
571    * {@code "uriAuthority"}, {@code "uriContext"}, {@code "uriRelativity"}, and {@code "uriResolution"}.
572    * Each entry is SVL-resolved then comma-split. Prevents the named property from inheriting values from
573    * parent {@code @Rest} annotations (router hierarchy). The {@code noInherit} attribute itself is never inherited.
574    *
575    * <h5 class='section'>Mixin sub-contexts (since 10.0.0)</h5>
576    * <p>
577    * On a class declared via {@link #mixins() @Rest(mixins=...)} on a host, {@code noInherit} also blocks the
578    * host-to-mixin inheritance walk for the named property.  The token set extends to every contribution list
579    * exposed by {@code @Rest}: {@code "serializers"}, {@code "parsers"}, {@code "encoders"}, {@code "converters"},
580    * {@code "responseProcessors"}, {@code "restOpArgs"}, {@code "guards"},
581    * {@code "partSerializer"}, {@code "partParser"}, and
582    * {@code "messages"}.  For example, {@code @Rest(noInherit={"guards"})} on a mixin removes the host's guard
583    * chain from the mixin's endpoints (typical pattern for deliberately-unguarded probes like
584    * {@code HealthMixin}).
585    *
586    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
587    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/SessionOptions">Session Options</a>
588    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerMixinSubContexts">REST Server &mdash; Mixin Sub-Contexts</a> (for the per-property opt-out semantics)
589    * </ul>
590    *
591    * @return The annotation value.
592    */

773   /**
774    * Disable content URL parameter.
775    *
776    * <p>
777    * When enabled (the default &mdash; this attribute is <jk>false</jk> unless explicitly set), the HTTP request
778    * content on PUT and POST requests can be passed in as text using the <js>"content"</js> URL parameter, letting
779    * a caller exercise an endpoint's body-consuming logic straight from a URL (handy for a quick manual test or a
780    * bookmarked link) without an actual PUT/POST body.
781    * <br>
782    * For example:
783    * <p class='burlenc'>
784    *  ?content=(name='John%20Smith',age=45)
785    * </p>
786    *
787    * <p>
788    * Because the override is on by default, treat it the same way as any other feature that lets untrusted URL
789    * content reach parsing/business logic: a link to a PUT/POST endpoint with a crafted <js>"content"</js>
790    * parameter is just as reproducible by a third party (e.g. embedded in a page that an authenticated user
791    * happens to load) as the equivalent real request body would be. The override is deliberately restricted to
792    * <c>PUT</c>/<c>POST</c> methods so that a simple cross-origin <c>GET</c> (the kind a browser issues with no
793    * preflight and no caller-controlled header for something as ordinary as an <code>&lt;img src=...&gt;</code>
794    * tag) can never trigger it this way, but resources that don't already validate that PUT/POST submissions are
795    * same-site in origin (e.g. with a token check, a custom-header check, or <c>SameSite</c> cookies) gain no
796    * additional protection here. Set this to <jk>true</jk> to disable the override entirely on any resource
797    * where it isn't a deliberate feature.
798    *
799    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
800    *    <li class='note'>
801    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
802    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
803    * </ul>
804    *
805    * @return The annotation value.
806    */
807   String disableContentParam() default "";
808
809   /**
810    * Opt the resource into <a class="doclink" href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7807">RFC 7807</a> /
811    * <a class="doclink" href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457">RFC 9457</a>
812    * {@code application/problem+json} error responses.
813    *
814    * <p>
815    * When enabled, the resource:
816    * <ul class='spaced-list'>
817    *    <li>Emits {@code application/problem+json} for thrown {@code BasicHttpException}s &mdash; regardless of the
818    *       client's {@code Accept} header. The body is a serialized
819    *       {@link org.apache.juneau.bean.rfc7807.Problem} populated from the exception's status code, reason phrase,
820    *       and message.
821    *    <li>Honors the client's {@code Accept} header on the success path. When a {@code @RestOp} method returns a
822    *       {@link org.apache.juneau.bean.rfc7807.Problem} (or throws a
823    *       {@link org.apache.juneau.bean.rfc7807.ProblemException}), the
824    *       {@link ProblemDetailsProcessor} only serializes it as
825    *       {@code application/problem+json} when the {@code Accept} header matches that media type (or {@code *&#47;*}).
826    * </ul>
827    *
828    * <ul class='values'>
829    *    <li><js>"true"</js> &mdash; enable problem-details responses for this resource.
830    *    <li><js>"false"</js> &mdash; disable problem-details responses for this resource (overrides an inherited
831    *       {@code "true"} from a parent {@code @Rest}).
832    *    <li><js>""</js> (default) &mdash; inherit from the next-most-derived {@code @Rest} in the resource-class
833    *       hierarchy. Default behavior (no opt-in anywhere in the chain) is unchanged from prior releases.
834    * </ul>
835    *
836    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
837    *    <li class='note'>
838    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
839    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
840    *    <li class='note'>
841    *       Use {@link #noInherit()} to prevent inheriting an opt-in from a parent {@code @Rest}.
842    * </ul>
843    *
844    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
845    *    <li class='jc'>{@link org.apache.juneau.bean.rfc7807.Problem}
846    *    <li class='jc'>{@link org.apache.juneau.bean.rfc7807.ProblemException}
847    *    <li class='jc'>{@link ProblemDetailsProcessor}
848    * </ul>
849    *
850    * @return The annotation value.
851    */
852   String problemDetails() default "";

854   /**
855    * Opt the resource into REST-driven serializer/parser debug behavior.
856    *
857    * <p>
858    * When enabled, the REST layer forces {@code Context.debug} on the serializer/parser sessions it creates to handle
859    * requests for this resource &mdash; engaging recursion-detection-that-throws (a genuine cycle throws
860    * {@code MarshallingRecursionException} instead of being size-guard-truncated), parse-input buffering (parse errors
861    * can quote the offending input), and stack-trace-prefixed marshalling exceptions.
862    *
863    * <p>
864    * This is a <b>behavior</b> switch, independent of the JUL logger level: raising a logger to
865    * {@link java.util.logging.Level#FINE FINE}/{@link java.util.logging.Level#FINEST FINEST} changes logging verbosity
866    * only and never changes marshalling behavior. A serializer/parser configured with {@code Context.debug} directly
867    * is unaffected by this setting.
868    *
869    * <ul class='values'>
870    *    <li><js>"true"</js> &mdash; enable marshalling debug for this resource.
871    *    <li><js>"false"</js> &mdash; disable marshalling debug for this resource (overrides an inherited
872    *       {@code "true"} from a parent {@code @Rest}).
873    *    <li><js>""</js> (default) &mdash; inherit from the next-most-derived {@code @Rest} in the resource-class
874    *       hierarchy. Default behavior (no opt-in anywhere in the chain) is marshalling debug OFF.
875    * </ul>
876    *
877    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
878    *    <li class='note'>
879    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
880    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
881    *    <li class='note'>
882    *       Use {@link #noInherit()} to prevent inheriting an opt-in from a parent {@code @Rest}.
883    * </ul>
884    *
885    * @return The annotation value.
886    */
887   String debugMarshalling() default "";
888
889   /**
890    * Opt this resource into per-request virtual-thread dispatch (Java 21+).
891    *
892    * <p>
893    * When enabled, every {@code @RestOp}-annotated handler invocation on this resource is submitted to a
894    * {@code Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()} virtual-thread-per-task executor
895    * lazily built by the {@link RestContext}. The platform request thread blocks on
896    * the virtual thread's completion (so the handler's return value, exceptions, and observability hooks are
897    * preserved verbatim), but blocking I/O inside the handler now parks a virtual thread instead of the
898    * carrier — i.e. the carrier thread is freed to service other concurrent requests while the handler is
899    * parked on socket / file / lock waits. Combined with {@link java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture}
900    * return types ({@code @RestGet} / {@code @RestPost} returning {@code CompletableFuture<T>}) this is the
901    * high-throughput pattern.
902    *
903    * <p>
904    * <b>Graceful degradation on Java 17/18/19/20:</b> the flag is detected during {@code RestContext}
905    * initialization. If the runtime is older than Java 21, a one-shot {@code WARNING} is logged and the
906    * resource falls back to the standard caller-thread dispatch path — no runtime error.
907    *
908    * <p>
909    * Per-{@code @RestOp} overrides are available via {@link RestOp#virtualThreads()}; the op-level setting
910    * takes precedence over the resource-level setting.
911    *
912    * <ul class='values'>
913    *    <li><js>"true"</js> &mdash; enable virtual-thread dispatch on Java 21+ (silently disabled on older JVMs).
914    *    <li><js>"false"</js> &mdash; explicitly disable.
915    *    <li><js>""</js> (default) &mdash; inherit from the next-most-derived {@code @Rest} in the resource-class
916    *       hierarchy.
917    * </ul>
918    *
919    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
920    *    <li class='note'>
921    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
922    *       (e.g. <js>"$E{ENABLE_VIRTUAL_THREADS,false}"</js>).
923    *    <li class='note'>
924    *       Synchronized blocks and JNI calls in handler code <i>pin</i> a virtual thread to its carrier thread
925    *       — prefer {@link java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock} over {@code synchronized} in handlers run
926    *       under this flag.
927    * </ul>
928    *
929    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
930    *    <li class='ja'>{@link RestOp#virtualThreads()}
931    * </ul>
932    *
933    * @return The annotation value.
934    */
935   String virtualThreads() default "";
936
937   /**
938    * Per-resource observability opt-in / opt-out control.
939    *
940    * <p>
941    * Controls whether the observability block ({@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.metrics.MetricsRecorder} /
942    * {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.tracing.TracerHook}) fires for operations on this resource.
943    * Per-operation overrides are available via {@link RestOp#observability()} (and the verb annotations).
944    *
945    * <ul class='values'>
946    *    <li><js>"true"</js> &mdash; strict opt-in: the resource <em>requires</em> a wired observability backend.
947    *       If neither a {@code @Bean MetricsRecorder} nor a {@code @Bean TracerHook} is registered when the
948    *       {@link RestContext} is built, construction fails with a precise error.
949    *       All operations on this resource have observability enabled.
950    *    <li><js>"false"</js> &mdash; explicit opt-out: the observability block is short-circuited for every
951    *       operation on this resource, even when a wired backend is present. Also suppresses
952    *       {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.tracing.TraceContextResponseProcessor} header injection for this resource.
953    *    <li><js>""</js> (default) &mdash; inherits the existing behavior: the observability block runs per-op,
954    *       but a missing {@code @Bean} silently falls back to the NoOp singleton — no startup error.
955    * </ul>
956    *
957    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
958    *    <li class='note'>
959    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
960    *       (e.g. <js>"$E{ENABLE_OBSERVABILITY,false}"</js>).
961    *    <li class='note'>
962    *       Per-operation overrides via {@link RestOp#observability()} (or verb annotations) take precedence over
963    *       this resource-level setting.
964    * </ul>
965    *
966    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
967    *    <li class='ja'>{@link RestOp#observability()}
968    *    <li class='jc'>{@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.metrics.MetricsRecorder}
969    *    <li class='jc'>{@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.tracing.TracerHook}
970    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerObservability">REST Server &mdash; Observability</a>
971    * </ul>
972    *
973    * @return The annotation value.
974    * @since 10.0.0
975    */
976   String observability() default "";

978   /**
979    * Configurable timeout (milliseconds) applied to {@link java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture}-returning
980    * handlers by {@link AsyncResponseProcessor}. Default is 30,000 ms.
981    *
982    * <p>
983    * On timeout, the future is cancelled with {@code mayInterruptIfRunning=true} and the response is
984    * committed as {@code 504 Gateway Timeout}. Set to {@code "0"} to disable the timeout entirely.
985    *
986    * <p>
987    * Per-{@code @RestOp} overrides are available via {@link RestOp#asyncTimeoutMillis()}; the op-level
988    * setting takes precedence over the resource-level setting.
989    *
990    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
991    *    <li class='note'>
992    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
993    *       (e.g. <js>"$E{ASYNC_TIMEOUT_MS,30000}"</js>).
994    * </ul>
995    *
996    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
997    *    <li class='jc'>{@link AsyncResponseProcessor}
998    *    <li class='ja'>{@link RestOp#asyncTimeoutMillis()}
999    * </ul>
1000    *
1001    * @return The annotation value.
1002    * @since 10.0.0
1003    */
1004   String asyncTimeoutMillis() default "";
1005
1006   /**
1007    * Names the {@link java.util.concurrent.Executor} bean used to route {@link java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture}
1008    * completion callbacks through a dedicated thread pool.
1009    *
1010    * <p>
1011    * When set, the {@link AsyncResponseProcessor} switches from
1012    * {@code future.whenComplete(callback)} to {@code future.whenCompleteAsync(callback, executor)}, so the
1013    * response-handler work runs on the named pool instead of the future's natural completion thread (often an
1014    * I/O-driver or database-callback thread).
1015    *
1016    * <p>
1017    * The value is the {@link org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.Bean#name() @Bean(name=...)} lookup key for an
1018    * {@link java.util.concurrent.Executor} registered in the resource's bean store.  Empty string (default)
1019    * means no override — completion callbacks run on the future's natural thread (the existing behavior).
1020    *
1021    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1022    * <p class='bjava'>
1023    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(path=<js>"/api"</js>, asyncCompletionExecutor=<js>"myCompletionPool"</js>)
1024    *    <jk>public class</jk> ApiResource <jk>extends</jk> RestServlet {
1025    *
1026    *       <ja>@Bean</ja>(name=<js>"myCompletionPool"</js>)
1027    *       <jk>public</jk> Executor completionPool() {
1028    *          <jk>return</jk> Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
1029    *       }
1030    *
1031    *       <ja>@RestGet</ja>(<js>"/orders/{id}"</js>)
1032    *       <jk>public</jk> CompletableFuture&lt;Order&gt; getOrder(<ja>@Path</ja> String id) {
1033    *          <jk>return</jk> orderService.fetchAsync(id); <jc>// callback runs on myCompletionPool</jc>
1034    *       }
1035    *    }
1036    * </p>
1037    *
1038    * <p>
1039    * Per-operation overrides are available via {@link RestOp#asyncCompletionExecutor()} (and the verb annotations).
1040    * A reference to a bean name that does not resolve in the bean store causes a startup failure.
1041    *
1042    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1043    *    <li class='note'>
1044    *       MDC propagation still works when this executor is set — the
1045    *       {@link MdcAsyncListener} wraps the callback <em>before</em> it is
1046    *       routed through the executor, so the MDC snapshot is restored on whichever thread the executor picks.
1047    * </ul>
1048    *
1049    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1050    *    <li class='jc'>{@link AsyncResponseProcessor}
1051    *    <li class='ja'>{@link RestOp#asyncCompletionExecutor()}
1052    * </ul>
1053    *
1054    * @return The annotation value.
1055    * @since 10.0.0
1056    */
1057   String asyncCompletionExecutor() default "";
1058
1059   /**
1060    * Specifies the compression encoders for this resource.
1061    *
1062    * <p>
1063    * Encoders are used to enable various kinds of compression (e.g. <js>"gzip"</js>) on requests and responses.
1064    *
1065    * <p>
1066    * Encoders are automatically inherited from {@link Rest#encoders()} annotations on parent classes with the encoders on child classes
1067    * prepended to the encoder group.
1068    * The {@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.encoders.EncoderSet.NoInherit EncoderSet.NoInherit} class can be used to prevent inheriting from the parent class.
1069    *
1070    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1071    * <p class='bjava'>
1072    *    <jc>// Define a REST resource that handles GZIP compression.</jc>
1073    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1074    *       encoders={
1075    *          GzipEncoder.<jk>class</jk>
1076    *       }
1077    *    )
1078    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource {
1079    *       ...
1080    *    }
1081    * </p>
1082    *
1083    * <p>
1084    * The encoders can also be tailored at the method level using {@link RestOp#encoders()} (and related annotations).

1088    * {@link org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.Bean @Bean(name="encoders")}.

1090    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
1091    * <ul>
1092    *    <li>Encoders on child are combined with those on parent class.
1093    * </ul>
1094    *
1095    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1096    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerEncoders">Encoders</a>
1097    * </ul>
1098    *
1099    * @return The annotation value.
1100    */
1101   Class<? extends Encoder>[] encoders() default {};

1133    *    <li>Guards are executed child-to-parent in the order they appear in the annotation.

1163   /**
1164    * The maximum allowed input size (in bytes) on HTTP requests.
1165    *
1166    * <p>
1167    * Useful for alleviating DoS attacks by throwing an exception when too much input is received instead of resulting
1168    * in out-of-memory errors which could affect system stability.
1169    *
1170    * <p>
1171    * Applies uniformly across body-reading paths, including {@code multipart/form-data} uploads: a request whose
1172    * declared {@code Content-Length} or parsed part sizes exceed this ceiling is rejected with a {@code 413}
1173    * response before (or as soon as) the oversized content would otherwise be buffered.
1174    *
1175    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1176    *    <li class='note'>
1177    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
1178    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
1179    * </ul>
1180    *
1181    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1182    *    <li class='ja'>{@link RestOp#maxInput}
1183    *    <li class='ja'>{@link RestPost#maxInput}
1184    *    <li class='ja'>{@link RestPut#maxInput}
1185    * </ul>
1186    *
1187    * @return The annotation value.
1188    */
1189   String maxInput() default "";

1191   /**
1192    * Messages.
1193    *
1194    * Identifies the location of the resource bundle for this class.
1195    *
1196    * <p>
1197    * There are two possible formats:
1198    * <ul>
1199    *    <li>A simple string - Represents the {@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.cp.Messages.Builder#name(String) name} of the resource bundle.
1200    *       <br><br><i>Example:</i>
1201    *       <p class='bjava'>
1202    *    <jc>// Bundle name is Messages.properties.</jc>
1203    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(messages=<js>"Messages"</js>)
1204    *       </p>
1205    *    <li>Simplified JSON - Represents parameters for the {@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.cp.Messages.Builder} class.
1206    *       <br><br><i>Example:</i>
1207    *       <p class='bjava'>
1208    *    <jc>// Bundles can be found in two packages.</jc>
1209    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(messages=<js>"{name:'Messages',baseNames:['{package}.{name}','{package}.i18n.{name}']"</js>)
1210    *       </p>
1211    * </ul>
1212    *
1213    * <p>
1214    * If the bundle name is not specified, the class name of the resource object is used.
1215    *
1216    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1217    *    <li class='note'>
1218    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
1219    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
1220    * </ul>
1221    *
1222    * @return The annotation value.
1223    */
1224   String messages() default "";

1226   /**
1227    * Specifies the parsers for converting HTTP request bodies into POJOs.
1228    *
1229    * <p>
1230    * Parsers are used to convert the content of HTTP requests into POJOs.
1231    * <br>Any of the Juneau framework parsers can be used in this setting.
1232    * <br>The parser selected is based on the request <c>Content-Type</c> header matched against the values returned by the following method
1233    * using a best-match algorithm:
1234    * <ul class='javatree'>
1235    *    <li class='jm'>{@link Parser#getMediaTypes()}
1236    * </ul>
1237    *
1238    * <p>
1239    * Parsers are automatically inherited from {@link Rest#parsers()} annotations on parent classes with the parsers on child classes
1240    * prepended to the parser group.
1241    * The {@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.parser.ParserSet.NoInherit ParserSet.NoInherit} class can be used to prevent inheriting from the parent class.
1242    *
1243    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1244    * <p class='bjava'>
1245    *    <jc>// Define a REST resource that can consume JSON and XML.</jc>
1246    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1247    *       parsers={
1248    *          JsonParser.<jk>class</jk>,
1249    *          XmlParser.<jk>class</jk>
1250    *       }
1251    *    )
1252    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource {
1253    *       ...
1254    *    }
1255    * </p>
1256    *
1257    * <p>
1258    * The parsers can also be tailored at the method level using {@link RestOp#parsers()} (and related annotations).
1259    *
1260    * <p>
1261    * For programmatic equivalents, contribute a {@link ParserSet} bean via
1262    * {@link org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.Bean @Bean(name="parsers")}.
1263    *
1264    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
1265    * <ul>
1266    *    <li>Parsers on child override those on parent class.
1267    *    <li>{@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.parser.ParserSet.Inherit ParserSet.Inherit} class can be used to inherit and augment values from parent.
1268    *    <li>{@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.parser.ParserSet.NoInherit ParserSet.NoInherit} class can be used to suppress inheriting from parent.
1269    *    <li>Parsers on methods take precedence over those on classes.
1270    * </ul>
1271    *
1272    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1273    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Marshalling">Marshalling</a>
1274    * </ul>
1275    *
1276    * @return The annotation value.
1277    */
1278   Class<?>[] parsers() default {};

1300   /**
1301    * Resource path.
1302    *
1303    * <p>
1304    * Used in the following situations:
1305    * <ul class='spaced-list'>
1306    *    <li>
1307    *       On child resources (resource classes attached to parents via the {@link #children()} annotation) to identify
1308    *       the subpath used to access the child resource relative to the parent.
1309    *    <li>
1310    *       On top-level {@link RestServlet} classes deployed as Spring beans when <c>JuneauRestInitializer</c> is being used.
1311    * </ul>
1312    *
1313    * <h5 class='topic'>On child resources</h5>
1314    * <p>
1315    * The typical usage is to define a path to a child resource relative to the parent resource.
1316    *
1317    * <h5 class='figure'>Example:</h5>
1318    * <p class='bjava'>
1319    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1320    *       children={ChildResource.<jk>class</jk>}
1321    *    )
1322    *    <jk>public class</jk> TopLevelResource <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {...}
1323    *
1324    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1325    *    path=<js>"/child"</js>,
1326    *    children={GrandchildResource.<jk>class</jk>}
1327    * )
1328    * <jk>public class</jk> ChildResource {...}
1329    *
1330    * <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1331    *    path=<js>"/grandchild"</js>
1332    * )
1333    * <jk>public class</jk> GrandchildResource {
1334    *    <ja>@RestGet</ja>(<js>"/"</js>)
1335    *    <jk>public</jk> String sayHello() {
1336    *       <jk>return</jk> <js>"Hello!"</js>;
1337    *    }
1338    * }
1339    * </p>
1340    * <p>
1341    * In the example above, assuming the <c>TopLevelResource</c> servlet is deployed to path <c>/myContext/myServlet</c>,
1342    * then the <c>sayHello</c> method is accessible through the URI <c>/myContext/myServlet/child/grandchild</c>.
1343    *
1344    * <p>
1345    * Note that in this scenario, the <c>path</c> attribute is not defined on the top-level resource.
1346    * Specifying the path on the top-level resource has no effect, but can be used for readability purposes.
1347    *
1348    * <h5 class='topic'>Path variables</h5>
1349    * <p>
1350    * The path can contain variables that get resolved to {@link Path @Path} parameters
1351    * or access through the {@link RestRequest#getPathParams()} method.
1352    *
1353    * <h5 class='figure'>Example:</h5>
1354    * <p class='bjava'>
1355    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1356    *       path=<js>"/myResource/{foo}/{bar}"</js>
1357    *    )
1358    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {
1359    *
1360    *    <ja>@RestGet</ja>(<js>"/{baz}"</js>)
1361    *    <jk>public void</jk> String doX(<ja>@Path</ja> String <jv>foo</jv>, <ja>@Path</ja> <jk>int</jk> <jv>bar</jv>, <ja>@Path</ja> MyPojo <jv>baz</jv>) {
1362    *       ...
1363    *    }
1364    *    }
1365    * </p>
1366    *
1367    * <p>
1368    * Variables can be used on either top-level or child resources and can be defined on multiple levels.
1369    *
1370    * <p>
1371    * All variables in the path must be specified or else the target will not resolve and a <c>404</c> will result.
1372    *
1373    * <p>
1374    * When variables are used on a path of a top-level resource deployed as a Spring bean in a Spring Boot application,
1375    * the first part of the URL must be a literal which will be used as the servlet path of the registered servlet.
1376    *
1377    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1378    *    <li class='note'>
1379    *       The leading slash is optional.  <js>"/myResource"</js> and <js>"myResource"</js> is equivalent.
1380    *    <li class='note'>
1381    *       The paths <js>"/myResource"</js> and <js>"/myResource/*"</js> are equivalent.
1382    *    <li class='note'>
1383    *       Paths must not end with <js>"/"</js> (per the servlet spec).
1384    *    <li class='note'>
1385    *       Effective only when this class is registered directly with the servlet container as a top-level
1386    *       resource.  When this class is imported as a mixin via {@code @Rest(mixins=...)}, the importing
1387    *       host's own {@code path()} or {@link #paths()} governs the mount and this annotation is silently
1388    *       ignored &mdash; mixin endpoints land in the host's URL namespace.
1389    * </ul>
1390    *
1391    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
1392    * <ul>
1393    *    <li>Path is searched for in child-to-parent order.
1394    * </ul>
1395    *
1396    * @return The annotation value.
1397    */
1398   String path() default "";
1399
1400   /**
1401    * Additional servlet mount paths.
1402    *
1403    * <p>
1404    * Optional multi-mount companion to {@link #path()} for top-level servlet deployment.
1405    *
1406    * <p>
1407    * When specified, servlet containers may mount this resource on each listed path.
1408    * This is primarily intended for built-in support endpoints such as health probes where multiple exact URLs
1409    * should be served by a single servlet instance.
1410    *
1411    * <h5 class='section'>Runtime substitution (since 10.0.0)</h5>
1412    * <p>
1413    * Each array element is treated as a template:
1414    * <ol>
1415    *    <li>The element runs through
1416    *       <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL</a>
1417    *       variable substitution (e.g. {@code $C{health.paths}}, {@code $E{HEALTH_PATHS,/healthz}},
1418    *       {@code $S{my.system.prop,/healthz}}) using the bootstrap {@link org.apache.juneau.commons.svl.VarResolver
1419    *       VarResolver} on the bean store.
1420    *    <li>The post-SVL value is split on {@code ,}; each piece is trimmed and empty pieces are dropped.
1421    *       A single template element can therefore expand to zero, one, or many mount paths.
1422    * </ol>
1423    *
1424    * <h5 class='figure'>Examples:</h5>
1425    * <p class='bjava'>
1426    *    <jc>// 1. Single key resolving to a multi-value config string.</jc>
1427    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(paths={<js>"$C{health.paths}"</js>})
1428    *
1429    *    <jc>// 2. Mix literal + resolved element.</jc>
1430    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(paths={<js>"/api"</js>, <js>"$C{extra.paths}"</js>})
1431    *
1432    *    <jc>// 3. Env var with comma-separated defaults baked in.</jc>
1433    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(paths={<js>"$E{HEALTH_PATHS,/healthz,/readyz}"</js>})
1434    * </p>
1435    *
1436    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1437    *    <li class='note'>
1438    *       Paths are normalized to servlet path-specs by the hosting runtime.
1439    *    <li class='note'>
1440    *       When both {@link #path()} and {@link #paths()} are present, runtimes may use {@link #paths()} for
1441    *       top-level mounting and continue using {@link #path()} for child-resource composition.
1442    *    <li class='note'>
1443    *       The annotation default sits at the lowest rung of the runtime-override resolution chain &mdash; see
1444    *       {@link RestContext#getPaths()} for the full precedence order (programmatic &gt; getter &gt; annotation).
1445    *    <li class='note'>
1446    *       An SVL failure (unresolved variable with no default) falls back to the literal element rather than
1447    *       throwing during construction.
1448    *    <li class='note'>
1449    *       Effective only when this class is registered directly with the servlet container as a top-level
1450    *       resource.  When this class is imported as a mixin via {@code @Rest(mixins=...)}, the importing
1451    *       host's own {@link #path()} or {@code paths()} governs the mount and this annotation is silently
1452    *       ignored &mdash; mixin endpoints land in the host's URL namespace.
1453    * </ul>
1454    *
1455    * @return The annotation value.
1456    */
1457   String[] paths() default {};
1458
1459   /**
1460    * Default path parameter definitions.
1461    *
1462    * <p>
1463    * Provides default values for {@link Path @Path} annotations on method parameters across all methods in this class.
1464    *
1465    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1466    * <p class='bjava'>
1467    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1468    *       pathParams={
1469    *          <ja>@Path</ja>(name=<js>"version"</js>, def=<js>"v1"</js>)
1470    *       }
1471    *    )
1472    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource {...}
1473    * </p>
1474    *
1475    * @return The annotation value.
1476    * @since 9.2.0
1477    */
1478   Path[] pathParams() default {};
1479
1480   /**
1481    * Supported accept media types.
1482    *
1483    * <p>
1484    * Overrides the media types inferred from the serializers that identify what media types can be produced by the resource.
1485    *
1486    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1487    *    <li class='note'>
1488    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
1489    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
1490    * </ul>
1491    *
1492    * @return The annotation value.
1493    */
1494   String[] produces() default {};
1495
1496   /**
1497    * Default query parameter definitions.
1498    *
1499    * <p>
1500    * Provides default values for {@link Query @Query} annotations on method parameters across all methods in this class.
1501    * Values specified here are used as defaults when the same property is not explicitly defined on a method parameter's
1502    * {@link Query @Query} annotation.
1503    *
1504    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1505    * <p class='bjava'>
1506    *    <jc>// Define common query parameters at class level</jc>
1507    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1508    *       queryParams={
1509    *          <ja>@Query</ja>(name=<js>"format"</js>, def=<js>"json"</js>, description=<js>"Output format"</js>),
1510    *          <ja>@Query</ja>(name=<js>"verbose"</js>, def=<js>"false"</js>, schema=<ja>@Schema</ja>(type=<js>"boolean"</js>))
1511    *       }
1512    *    )
1513    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource {
1514    *
1515    *       <jc>// Method will inherit the default query parameter definitions</jc>
1516    *       <ja>@RestGet</ja>
1517    *       <jk>public</jk> String doGet(<ja>@Query</ja>(<js>"format"</js>) String format, <ja>@Query</ja>(<js>"verbose"</js>) <jk>boolean</jk> verbose) {...}
1518    *
1519    *       <jc>// Can override defaults on a per-method basis</jc>
1520    *       <ja>@RestGet</ja>
1521    *       <jk>public</jk> String doGet2(<ja>@Query</ja>(name=<js>"format"</js>, def=<js>"xml"</js>) String format) {...}
1522    *    }
1523    * </p>
1524    *
1525    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1526    *    <li class='note'>
1527    *       These defaults apply to validation, parsing, and OpenAPI/Swagger documentation generation.
1528    *    <li class='note'>
1529    *       Method-level {@link Query @Query} annotations take precedence over class-level definitions.
1530    *    <li class='note'>
1531    *       The {@link Query#name() name} attribute must be specified for each query definition.
1532    * </ul>
1533    *
1534    * @return The annotation value.
1535    * @since 9.2.0
1536    */
1537   Query[] queryParams() default {};
1538
1539   /**
1540    * Render response stack traces in responses.
1541    *
1542    * <p>
1543    * Render stack traces in HTTP response bodies when errors occur.
1544    *
1545    * <p>
1546    * Off by default. Besides the stack trace itself, this same setting also determines whether the
1547    * {@code Thrown} response header is set and whether an error whose exception type wasn't deliberately
1548    * thrown by application code (i.e. not a {@link org.apache.juneau.http.response.BasicHttpException
1549    * BasicHttpException} or one of its subclasses) has its class name/message echoed into the error body.
1550    * Leave this off in production so that an unplanned exception type (a database driver error, a
1551    * file-system exception, and the like) can't incidentally leak implementation detail to the caller;
1552    * turn it on only for local debugging.
1553    *
1554    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1555    *    <li class='note'>
1556    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
1557    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
1558    * </ul>
1559    *
1560    * @return The annotation value.
1561    */
1562   String renderResponseStackTraces() default "";
1563
1564   /**
1565    * Response processors.
1566    *
1567    * <p>
1568    * Specifies a list of {@link ResponseProcessor} classes that know how to convert POJOs returned by REST methods or
1569    * set via {@link RestResponse#setContent(Object)} into appropriate HTTP responses.
1570    *
1571    * <p>
1572    * These processors run in order and are the extension point that turns a method's return value into the response
1573    * body.  The built-in {@link SerializedPojoProcessor} is the default POJO handler &mdash; it runs the
1574    * content-negotiated {@link #serializers() serializer}, so for ordinary POJO returns the effective response format
1575    * is governed by serializer ordering and the request <c>Accept</c> header (see {@link #serializers()}), not by this
1576    * list.
1577    *
1578    * <p>
1579    * A custom view-renderer {@link ResponseProcessor} installed here (for example a template-rendering processor
1580    * contributed by a view mixin &mdash; see {@link #mergeResponseProcessorsIntoHost()}) can instead claim a return
1581    * value and render it directly (e.g. as HTML from a template) before serializer negotiation is reached, changing the
1582    * effective response for the returns it handles.
1583    *
1584    * @return The annotation value.
1585    */
1586   Class<? extends ResponseProcessor>[] responseProcessors() default {};
1587
1588   /**
1589    * Java REST operation method parameter resolvers.
1590    *
1591    * <p>
1592    * By default, the Juneau framework will automatically Java method parameters of various types (e.g.
1593    * <c>RestRequest</c>, <c>Accept</c>, <c>Reader</c>).
1594    * <br>This setting allows you to provide your own resolvers for your own class types that you want resolved.
1595    *
1596    * @return The annotation value.
1597    */
1598   Class<? extends RestOpArg>[] restOpArgs() default {};
1599
1600   /**
1601    * Role guard.
1602    *
1603    * <p>
1604    * An expression defining if a user with the specified roles are allowed to access methods on this class.
1605    *
1606    * <p>
1607    * This is a shortcut for specifying {@link RestOp#roleGuard()} on all the REST operations on a class.
1608    *
1609    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1610    * <p class='bjava'>
1611    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1612    *       path=<js>"/foo"</js>,
1613    *       roleGuard=<js>"ROLE_ADMIN || (ROLE_READ_WRITE &amp;&amp; ROLE_SPECIAL)"</js>
1614    *    )
1615    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {
1616    *       ...
1617    *    }
1618    * </p>
1619    *
1620    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1621    *    <li class='note'>
1622    *       Supports any of the following expression constructs:
1623    *       <ul>
1624    *          <li><js>"foo"</js> - Single arguments.
1625    *          <li><js>"foo,bar,baz"</js> - Multiple OR'ed arguments.
1626    *          <li><js>"foo | bar | baz"</js> - Multiple OR'ed arguments, pipe syntax.
1627    *          <li><js>"foo || bar || baz"</js> - Multiple OR'ed arguments, Java-OR syntax.
1628    *          <li><js>"fo*"</js> - Patterns including <js>'*'</js> and <js>'?'</js>.
1629    *          <li><js>"fo* &amp; *oo"</js> - Multiple AND'ed arguments, ampersand syntax.
1630    *          <li><js>"fo* &amp;&amp; *oo"</js> - Multiple AND'ed arguments, Java-AND syntax.
1631    *          <li><js>"fo* || (*oo || bar)"</js> - Parenthesis.
1632    *       </ul>
1633    *    <li>
1634    *       AND operations take precedence over OR operations (as expected).
1635    *    <li>
1636    *       Whitespace is ignored.
1637    *    <li>
1638    *       <jk>null</jk> or empty expressions always match as <jk>false</jk>.
1639    *    <li>
1640    *       If patterns are used, you must specify the list of declared roles using {@link #rolesDeclared()}.
1641    *    <li>
1642    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
1643    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
1644    * </ul>
1645    *
1646    * @return The annotation value.
1647    */
1648   String roleGuard() default "";
1649
1650   /**
1651    * Declared roles.
1652    *
1653    * <p>
1654    * A comma-delimited list of all possible user roles.
1655    *
1656    * <p>
1657    * Used in conjunction with {@link #roleGuard()} is used with patterns.
1658    *
1659    * <p>
1660    * This is a shortcut for specifying {@link RestOp#rolesDeclared()} on all the REST operations on a class.
1661    *
1662    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1663    * <p class='bjava'>
1664    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1665    *       rolesDeclared=<js>"ROLE_ADMIN,ROLE_READ_WRITE,ROLE_READ_ONLY,ROLE_SPECIAL"</js>,
1666    *       roleGuard=<js>"ROLE_ADMIN || (ROLE_READ_WRITE &amp;&amp; ROLE_SPECIAL)"</js>
1667    *    )
1668    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {
1669    *       ...
1670    *    }
1671    * </p>
1672    *
1673    * @return The annotation value.
1674    */
1675   String rolesDeclared() default "";
1676
1677   /**
1678    * Specifies the serializers for POJOs into HTTP response bodies.
1679    *
1680    * <p>
1681    * Serializer are used to convert POJOs to HTTP response bodies.
1682    * <br>Any of the Juneau framework serializers can be used in this setting.
1683    * <br>The serializer selected is based on the request <c>Accept</c> header matched against the values returned by the following method
1684    * using a best-match algorithm:
1685    * <ul class='javatree'>
1686    *    <li class='jm'>{@link Serializer#getMediaTypeRanges()}
1687    * </ul>
1688    *
1689    * <p>
1690    * <b>Ordering determines the default response format.</b>  A request that sends no <c>Accept</c> header (or a
1691    * non-specific one such as <c>*&#47;*</c>, which browsers send by default) is treated as <c>*&#47;*</c> and matches
1692    * the <b>first</b> serializer in this list.  That is why the default configuration
1693    * ({@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.config.BasicUniversalConfig}) lists HTML first &mdash; so a browser, or any
1694    * client that omits <c>Accept</c>, receives HTML rather than JSON.  Order this list deliberately, and send an
1695    * explicit <c>Accept: application/json</c> to force JSON regardless of ordering.
1696    *
1697    * <p>
1698    * Serializers are automatically inherited from {@link Rest#serializers()} annotations on parent classes with the serializers on child classes
1699    * prepended to the serializer group.
1700    * The {@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.serializer.SerializerSet.NoInherit SerializerSet.NoInherit} class can be used to prevent inheriting from the parent class.
1701    *
1702    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1703    * <p class='bjava'>
1704    *    <jc>// Define a REST resource that can produce JSON and XML.</jc>
1705    *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(
1706    *       serializers={
1707    *          JsonParser.<jk>class</jk>,
1708    *          XmlParser.<jk>class</jk>
1709    *       }
1710    *    )
1711    *    <jk>public class</jk> MyResource {
1712    *       ...
1713    *    }
1714    * </p>
1715    *
1716    * <p>
1717    * The serializers can also be tailored at the method level using {@link RestOp#serializers()} (and related annotations).
1718    *
1719    * <p>
1720    * For programmatic equivalents, contribute a {@link SerializerSet} bean via
1721    * {@link org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.Bean @Bean(name="serializers")}.
1722    *
1723    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
1724    * <ul>
1725    *    <li>Serializers on child override those on parent class.
1726    *    <li>{@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.serializer.SerializerSet.Inherit SerializerSet.Inherit} class can be used to inherit and augment values from parent.
1727    *    <li>{@link org.apache.juneau.marshall.serializer.SerializerSet.NoInherit SerializerSet.NoInherit} class can be used to suppress inheriting from parent.
1728    *    <li>Serializers on methods take precedence over those on classes.
1729    * </ul>
1730    *
1731    * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1732    *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Marshalling">Marshalling</a>
1733    * </ul>
1734    *
1735    * @return The annotation value.
1736    */
1737   Class<? extends Serializer>[] serializers() default {};
1738
1739   /**
1740    * Optional site name.
1741    *
1742    * <p>
1743    * The site name is intended to be a title that can be applied to the entire site.
1744    *
1745    * <p>
1746    * One possible use is if you want to add the same title to the top of all pages by defining a header on a
1747    * common parent class like so:
1748    * <p class='bjava'>
1749    *  <ja>@HtmlDocConfig</ja>(
1750    *       header={
1751    *          <js>"&lt;h1&gt;$RS{siteName}&lt;/h1&gt;"</js>,
1752    *          <js>"&lt;h2&gt;$RS{title}&lt;/h2&gt;"</js>
1753    *       }
1754    *    )
1755    * </p>
1756    *
1757    * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1758    *    <li class='note'>
1759    *       Supports <a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerSvlVariables">SVL Variables</a>
1760    *       (e.g. <js>"$L{my.localized.variable}"</js>).
1761    * </ul>
1762    *
1763    * @return The annotation value.
1764    */
1765   String siteName() default "";
1766
1767   /**
1768    * Static files.
1769    *
1770    * <p>
1771    * Used to retrieve localized files to be served up as static files through the REST API via the following
1772    * predefined methods:
1773    * <ul class='javatree'>
1774    *    <li class='jm'>{@code BasicRestResource.getHtdoc(String, Locale)}.
1775    *    <li class='jm'>{@code BasicRestServlet.getHtdoc(String, Locale)}.
1776    * </ul>
1777    *
1778    * <p>
1779    * The static file finder can be accessed through the following methods:
1780    * <ul class='javatree'>
1781    *    <li class='jm'>{@link RestContext#getStaticFiles()}
1782    * </ul>
1783    *
1784    * <h5 class='section'>Inheritance Rules</h5>
1785    * <ul>
1786    *    <li>Static files on child are combined with those on parent class.
1787    *    <li>Static files are are executed child-to-parent in the order they appear in the annotation.
1788    * </ul>
1789    *
1790    * @return The annotation value.
1791    */
1792   Class<? extends StaticFiles> staticFiles() default StaticFiles.Void.class;
